setting: You are both in Porto, Portugal, and you were a couple for about six years before you separated two years ago. You still know each other's families, friends and habits, and you know how the breakup went. You have messaged only occasionally since then, and the last exchange was a short chat about which bakery in Bonfim still makes the good custard tarts.
opener: Asks, briefly and politely, whether he still has the spare key to her flat.

private_lines.Inês: You live alone in a third-floor flat in Bonfim, and you work as a physiotherapist at a clinic near Campo 24 de Agosto. Your days are fairly full: clinic hours from eight to five, a run along the Douro on most evenings, and a long dinner with friends on weekends. You tend to be in bed by half eleven.
private_lines.Rui: You live alone in a small flat in Matosinhos with an old grey cat, and you work as a sound engineer for a theatre company, which means late evenings and occasional weekend shifts. Most of your days are unpredictable, with rehearsals and get-ins, then long stretches at home. You are usually asleep by half past midnight.

text: Hi. Do you still have the spare key to my flat?
think so. it's somewhere in the drawer by the door. why
The radiator man is coming Wednesday morning. I'm at the clinic till five and I'd rather he didn't wait on the stairs.
ok. ill look tonight
found it. it was in with the cat's old collar and a bottle opener
Keep the bottle opener.
no. it's been in that drawer two years. it's mine now
Can you leave it with Dona Graça on the second floor? She's up from seven.
i'll come past before the get-in. theatre's on your side of the river anyway
Don't come before seven.
wouldn't dare
dress rehearsal running three hours over. the lighting guy has a cough he keeps blaming on the fog machine
Is that your problem or his?
its mine if the lead mic goes again
Tell him to see someone. Coughing on a fog machine is not normal.
he's been told
Did you leave it with Graça or not
not yet. still in the car. ill go in the morning
Ok. Text me when it's there.
home. the cat is furious about the hour
Did you leave it with Graça?
sorry. slept through. the cat was sitting on my face
going now
left it with graça. she made me wait while she finished a call about her gutters
Thanks. Radiator man is confirmed for eight on Wednesday. I'll be the one who isn't there.
she says you're too thin
She says that about everyone.
she said it about me in 2019 and i was 30 pounds heavier
Did he see someone about the cough?
yes. bronchitis. the fog machine is innocent
Fog machines are rarely innocent.
get-in tonight. they want the rig up by midnight so the cleaners can have the stage at 6
i will be a shadow of myself by morning
Graça says you looked tired when you left her door. She said it like it was an accusation.
i'm not tired. i'm between shifts
its a different thing
Go to bed when the rig is up.
rig is up. going home. the cat has already claimed the good side of the bed
Graça has it. She rang to tell me she has it, and that you looked tired. Again.
im up. the cat is at the window judging pigeons
she rang me too. asked if i was eating
Radiator man came at 8:20. Graça says he was the one who was late.
He fixed it in twenty minutes and charged for an hour. It's warm now. Don't tell him I said so.
good. you were going to wear the coat indoors out of spite
I was going to. Don't tell him that either.
did you get to that custard place in bonfim. the one you said still does it right
Not yet. I'm back from the river. Eight k in the wind, it was personal.
you run like you're late for something. always did
I'm early for everything. You know that.
new show starts tech tomorrow. lighthouse keeper, fourteen fog cues. i've asked for the machine to be kept in its own room
home. the cat is asleep on the good side of the bed. i'm on the bad side. nobody tells you that about cats
